And despite efforts by the government and its partners, root causes of missed vaccination opportunities — instances where children eligible for vaccination visit health facilities but don’t receive required doses — remain largely unexplored.   In response, a study done through Sabin and the World Health Organization’s COVID-19 Recovery for Routine Immunization Programs Fellowship aimed to investigate exactly why these children were not getting vaccinated. post_message: “Caregivers used to wait for vaccine teams. Now they remind each other and bring their children early.”   Despite ongoing national and state immunization programs in #Nigeria, many children — especially in hard-to-reach and underserved communities — remain unvaccinated due to limited tracking systems, gender barriers, and weak community engagement.  As part of Sabin and WHO’s COVID-19 Recovery for Routine Immunization Programs Fellowship, a project was launched to identify and reach zero-dose children in Bauchi state. The project embraced a grassroots approach, emphasizing local knowledge, simple tools, and culturally sensitive strategies to strengthen outreach and accountability.  The project reached more than 300 children with needed vaccines, and left health workers in the area more equipped than ever to continue their work. Dive into the case study, led by Alawiyatu Usman Ibrahim. ⤵  https://bit.ly/4kbLgvG

post_message: “Caregivers used to wait for vaccine teams. Now they remind each other and bring their children early.”   Despite ongoing national and state immunization programs in #Nigeria, many children — especially in hard-to-reach and underserved communities — remain unvaccinated due to limited tracking systems, gender barriers, and weak community engagement.  As part of Sabin and WHO’s COVID-19 Recovery for Routine Immunization Programs Fellowship, a project was launched to identify and reach zero-dose children in Bauchi state. The project embraced a grassroots approach, emphasizing local knowledge, simple tools, and culturally sensitive strategies to strengthen outreach and accountability.  The project reached more than 300 children with needed vaccines, and left health workers in the area more equipped than ever to continue their work. post_message: #Guinea has faced persistent challenges in achieving high routine immunization coverage, a situation worsened by the COVID-19 pandemic.  And despite efforts by the government and its partners, root causes of missed vaccination opportunities — instances where children eligible for vaccination visit health facilities but don’t receive required doses — remain largely unexplored.   In response, a study done through Sabin and the World Health Organization’s COVID-19 Recovery for Routine Immunization Programs Fellowship aimed to investigate exactly why these children were not getting vaccinated.  Read the case study, written by Dr. Mamadou Saliou Baldé, which distills lessons learned about data collection, community outreach, parental misconceptions about vaccination, and more. ⤵  https://bit.ly/4kmYAxw
